acceptance: `go test -count=2 ./internal/bridge/` passes (red first: fails today on the second iteration)
No bridge test registers a driver in init(); every registry reset restores the previous set through t.Cleanup
fix: A test that needs a controlled driver set restores the previous registry with t.Cleanup (ResetDriversForTesting returns a restore func, or a snapshot-and-restore helper). The chatty driver registers inside its test with t.Cleanup unregistering it, not in init(). One home for snapshot-and-restore.
source: console, 2026-10-07 (seen during the C0 floor runs; pre-existing on main)
summary: `chattyTimeoutDriver` (go/internal/bridge/artifact_timeout_diag_test.go) registers itself in `init()`. Several bridge tests call `ResetDriversForTesting()` (codex_pretrust_launch_test.go, coverage_batch7_test.go, coverage_test.go, driver_tmux_repl_runscope_test.go), which clears the whole registry and never restores it. Under `-count=2` `init()` does not re-run, so `TestEngineLaunch_ArtifactTimeout_SummaryBeatsEarlierBridgeChatter` launches an unregistered CLI and fails; the test is order-dependent, which CI's `-count=1` hides.
title: A bridge test driver registered in init() is lost after ResetDriversForTesting (-count=2 fails)
